entries.3ffcccd91ce4184d: What is sold differs by the buyer's field. Building & Industrial covers standard pumps (land, submersible and water supply), refrigeration machinery and blowers, for building and industrial facilities. Energy covers custom pumps, compressors, turbines, cryopumps and expanders, for oil and gas, power and new energy. Infrastructure covers custom pumps for agricultural, drainage, and water and sewage use, and tunnel blowers, for water infrastructure. Environment covers municipal waste incineration plants, industrial waste incineration plants and water treatment plants, and in addition to engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) work, it also performs operation management and maintenance (O&M). Precision & Electronics covers vacuum pumps, CMP equipment, plating equipment and exhaust gas treatment equipment, for semiconductor manufacturing. After-sales service (called 'Service & Support' in the report) appears many times in explanations of order and sales trends in domestic Building & Industrial, Energy, and Precision & Electronics. As a common policy across the business, the report states that it aims to become a 'solutions provider' that collects and analyzes operating data from products delivered to customers and offers services such as energy saving, predictive failure management and operation guarantees. Consolidated R&D expenses were ¥23,233 million, of which Precision & Electronics had the largest share at ¥12,009 million among the five companies, and the company-wide technology policy lists fluid analysis and control, vibration and noise control, and interface control as core technologies. In November 2025, it entered into an agreement to acquire, among others, the three-phase motor and IPM motor business of [[company:mitsubishi-electric|Mitsubishi Electric Corporation]]. The transfer date is 'during fiscal 2026 (planned),' and as of the report, the transfer has not been completed.

entries.8a628750b78e5844: Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥958,285 million, up 10.6% from ¥866,668 million in the previous fiscal year. The securities report’s revenue recognition policy states that revenue from manufacturing and selling products is mainly recognized at the time of delivery or acceptance of the products. Construction contracts and maintenance contracts in Building & Industry, Energy, Infrastructure and Environment are recognized as revenue over the period of construction or maintenance, according to progress, if any of certain requirements are met. Progress is measured as the ratio of actual costs to estimated total costs. For Precision & Electronics, the securities report describes only the manufacture and sale of products (at delivery or acceptance) as its revenue recognition method and does not describe the treatment of maintenance services. As of December 31, 2025, receivables arising from contracts with customers were ¥207,582 million, contract assets recognized according to construction progress were ¥119,684 million, and contract liabilities, which are consideration received from customers for performance obligations not yet fulfilled, were ¥82,498 million (at the end of the previous fiscal year: ¥167,850 million, ¥116,792 million and ¥108,778 million, respectively). The same amount as the total order backlog of ¥912,020 million is printed in Note 28 as “transaction price allocated to unsatisfied performance obligations.” The securities report states that these performance obligations are expected to be completed and recognized as revenue mostly within three years for Building & Industry, Energy and Infrastructure, within 20 years for Environment, and within one year for Precision & Electronics.
